title: One scalar test when all boundary tangential directions are allowed
reviewed_arguments: H0--H1 retain a compact whole boundary, every allowed tangential equator direction, bounded complete families and exact common/varying input quantifiers.

Q0--Q2 construct an exact atlas model with bounded normal difference. Its fixed-frequency difference from identity has smooth tangential kernels with polynomial seminorms. Global squaring preserves target ellipticity and an exact deep model.
L0 retains the complete ordered parametrix, differential amplification and full cross-chart residual family.

L1 proves Hilbert representation by minimum norm, constructs the weak inverse, derives ordinary regularity, polynomial smooth seminorms and norm derivatives from the resolvent identity. No b-class assertion is made for that inverse.
L2--L3 localize before inversion; the actual differential commutator has interior input. Its transpose test seminorms have square-integrable output decay, giving the original Banach bound.
S0 uses the positive compact-normal floor and actual quotient Schur estimate. The middle normal operator is anisotropic, with no unsupported joint pseudodifferential claim.

S1 proves the sandwich is a full residual both at the front and in transition intervals. Polynomial tangential kernel bounds and Schwartz normal convolution control every differentiated complete kernel.
S2 retains exact normal-support margins. The complete commutator is an original smooth kernel with both projections compactly interior.
S3 transposes twice for the Banach quadratic-form estimate and uses the exact noncommuting scalar norm identity, rather than positivity alone.
P0--P1 recover the full normal regularizer by the complementary polynomial and its smooth interior error annulus. No discarded corner term is assigned an unproved coarse bound.

T0 gives A=(Q+iS)L^M on the whole manifold, with full class, compact projections, allowed microsupport and uniform differential-input quantifiers. T1 states only applicable observation and actual graph consequences.
The three solutions check a complementary scalar mode floor, exact exponential support buffers and a non-flat auxiliary inverse with sufficient L2 output test seminorms.
